subject: Follow-up: hosted API run-rate, spike tolerance, and unit economics
messages:
From: Alex Rios <alex@brightlane.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call

Rafael — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying points so we can lock a working estimate: 

- Expected monthly token volume (generation + embeddings): roughly 90M — 130M tokens. We expect the baseline daily traffic to sit near the low end for most of November/December and ramp in Q1.
- Typical sustained TPS during business hours: ~250–400 TPS (AML event processing + user chat).
- Short spikes: releases and marketing blasts will spike traffic; we anticipate rare bursts up to ~2,200 TPS for 3–8 minutes, maybe 6–8x our normal peak.
- Budget: looking to land in the $20–$30 / 1M-token window initially; target monthly spend in the $1.8k–$3.9k range depending on final consumption.

Open questions for you:
1) Would Redwood recommend a specific hosted tier or burst policy to handle those 2–3 minute spikes without huge unit-cost blowup?
2) Any suggestions on a short-term caching/prefix strategy to reduce downstream token generation for our release workflows?

Happy to share a sample hourly traffic CSV if that helps. Can we aim to lock a tentative pricing estimate by next Thursday?

— Alex
Platform Lead, Brightlane

On Fri, Nov 14, 2025 at 09:20 AM rafael_mendes@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks for the time today, Alex. Sending over the items we discussed (hosting tiers snapshot attached).
> -- Rafael

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Alex Rios <alex@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosted API run-rate, spike tolerance, and unit economics

Alex — really helpful summary, thanks. A couple quick answers and a request for one small data point so we can produce an accurate hosted estimate: 

1) Tier & spike handling: for a profile with sustained ~300 TPS and occasional short spikes to ~2.2k TPS, we typically recommend a Dedicated-like internal buffer on the hosted offering (we call it "burst lanes") plus a short TTL prefix cache for common release-related prompts. That combination keeps unit costs closer to baseline while absorbing 2–5 minute spikes.

2) Caching suggestions: a 30s prefix cache on release-check endpoints and a KV cache for reused system prompts usually removes ~10–25% of per-request tokens in our experience. If you can share a 48-hour sample of release traffic (even anonymized counts per minute), that will let us model spike tail behavior precisely.

Attached: hosted_tiers_snapshot.xlsx (quick mapping of our available bands + burst allowances).

Proposed next steps:
- You share 48h anonymized traffic sample (CSV) —> we run pricing sensitivity and return a 1-page estimate.
- We propose a technical sync (30m) next week to validate cacheable surfaces and identify short-term latency SLOs.

I’ll also loop in Karthik internally to review unit economics for the band you prefer. If that works, I’ll follow up with a concrete estimate.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 10:43:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up — Brightlane volume + spike profile (pricing sensitivity)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Alex's recap and our initial response. Key inputs we have: 90–130M mo, sustained 250–400 TPS, short spikes to ~2.2k TPS, target $20–$30 / 1M tokens.

My read: Brightlane's sensitivity is primarily on unit cost but they will tolerate a small overage for the first 60–90 days if we keep the spike exposure manageable. Two pricing levers to consider:
- Offer a tiered $/1M baseline with an explicit short-spike burst surcharge (metered per-minute above a 95th percentile threshold), or
- Lock a slightly higher committed unit price for a guaranteed burst allowance (e.g., commit to 100M/mo at $24/1M with included 10 minutes/day of spike capacity at 2.2k TPS).

Preliminary numbers I ran (attached pricing_sensitivity_model.csv):
- Scenario A (metered bursts): 100M tokens at $22/1M + metered spike minutes = est $2,200 + $350 spike surcharge/mo (varies)
- Scenario B (committed burst buffer): 100M tokens at $24/1M with 10min/day included spike allowance = est $2,400/mo (more predictable)

Recommend we present both options to the customer; highlight predictability vs unit-cost tradeoff. Karthik — can you confirm the SLA implications on offering the committed-burst buffer? Marissa — should we include a 10% introductory discount if they sign a 3-month commit?

— Rafael

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Alex Rios <alex@brightlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted estimate & next steps — Brightlane (90–130M tokens)

Alex — thanks for the traffic sample you sent earlier this morning. We ran a sensitivity sweep and put together a short estimate (attached: redwood-hosted-estimate-v3.pdf). High level: 

- Confirmed consumption band: 90M — 130M tokens / month.
- Baseline sustained TPS: 250–400 TPS; spikes modeled at 2,200 TPS lasting 3–8 minutes, 2–3x/month on average.
- Pricing options (summary):
  * Option 1 (metered bursts): $22 / 1M tokens baseline. Bursts billed per spike-minute above 95th percentile at $0.012 per spike-minute-TPS-unit (estimated $300–$500/mo in our model).
  * Option 2 (committed burst buffer): $24 / 1M tokens with an included burst allowance (10 min/day at up to 2.2k TPS). Modeled cost for 100M tokens = $2,400/mo (predictable).

Recommendation: for short ramp and unpredictable marketing spikes, Option 2 gives Brightlane predictable unit economics and simpler bookkeeping. If you expect the spikes to be extremely irregular and you want lower baseline, Option 1 keeps initial cost down but can produce variable month-to-month bills.

Next steps: 
- If Option 2 looks right, I’ll prepare a 3-month provisional commitment with an introductory 10% discount and a simple SLA addendum covering burst behavior.
- Let’s schedule a 30-minute technical sync next Tue/Wed to validate cacheable endpoints and test a staged spike in a sandbox.
- I’ve attached the estimate PDF and included a DocuSign link to turn the provisional commitment into a signed PO if you’re ready.

Please confirm preferred option and availability for next-week tech sync.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
